meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Atria CTO), Devon Park (ML Eng), Samir Lee (Ops)
summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Atria runs user-facing summarization and search models (~1M tokens/day) and is cost-sensitive. Discussed per-token pricing, batching and caching levers (KV/prefix caching), quantization impacts, and pilot benchmark. Agreed to share pricing spreadsheet and run a benchmark pilot targeting latency and cost targets.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, just to confirm names. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. Samir our solutions engineer is here too.
[00:10] Lena (Atria CTO): Hi Maya, hi Samir, Lena here. We run Atria Analytics — we do real-time summarization and semantic search for financial docs.
[00:18] Devon (Atria ML Eng): Devon here, handles models/pipelines.
[00:22] Samir (Redwood SE): Quick note, we'll dig into cost levers and a sample benchmark at the end. Is that ok?
[00:27] Lena: Yep, cost is the big gating factor.
[00:34] Speaker 1: Alright, can you give a quick run through of current architecture?
[00:38] Devon: Sure. We host models on AWS, mostly mixed — some managed endpoints on SageMaker for latency-critical requests, and batch jobs on EC2 for indexing. Our main workload is a low-latency summarization path, average prompt+response is 800 tokens roundtrip. We see about 35k requests/day, ~1M tokens/day total.
[00:58] Samir (Redwood SE): Nice detail — so roughly 1M tokens/day. Are those mostly generation or embeddings?
[01:05] Devon: 85% generation (summaries), 15% embeddings for similarity.
[01:10] Maya: Perfect. So the key levers we'll talk about are per-token pricing, batching to improve throughput, and caching (prefix/KV cache) to reduce duplicate generation. Also dedicated capacity can reduce unit cost if you have predictable volume.
[01:24] Lena: Can you unpack the per-token math? How much cheaper is dedicated vs hosted?
[01:30] Maya: Sure. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token rates — for our curated open models typical baseline is $X.XX per 1M tokens on hosted (note: placeholder; we'll send exact sheet). Dedicated is reserved capacity — unit cost can be 30-60% lower depending on commit and model. Private (VPC/on-prem) has higher up-front platform fees but gives control over infra and potentially lower infra-only costs.
[01:52] Devon: 30-60% is a big range. What's the break-even for us? We have ~1M tokens/day so roughly 30M/month.
[02:02] Samir (Redwood SE): Right, so math example — if hosted is $5 per 1M tokens (example), that's $150/month for 30M? Wait, math... (laughter) sorry. Actually $5 * 30 = $150  — oh that seems low, let me reframe: hosted per-token is often in the $X-$Y range. We'll provide an apples-to-apples. With dedicated, the amortized cost per token drops because of reserved GPU throughput; caching and batching further reduce effective tokens generated.
[02:29] Lena: We're particularly interested in batching and caching. Our requests are pretty spiky during market hours.
[02:34] Samir (Redwood SE): Batching helps when you can accept a few 10s of ms extra latency and combine requests into a single GPU batch. For many models, batching improves throughput by 2-6x depending on seq length. We also support dynamic batching windows. For latency-critical queries you can keep batch sizes small; for background you can push higher.
[02:52] Devon: And caching? How does Redwood do prefix/KV cache? We have a lot of near-duplicate prompts.
[02:58] Samir (Redwood SE): Two main caches — prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes, and KV (key-value) cache reuse across sessions. If you have similar prompts, prefix caching can shave off the decoder steps, reducing total tokens executed on GPU. In practice we see 10-40% token savings in workloads with repeated context. Note: transcription sometimes shows KV as K V cash in our notes.
[03:18] Lena: That 10-40% could swing our cost decisions. We need realistic numbers in our workload.
[03:22] Maya: Totally. That's why the benchmark pilot is helpful. We'll run a focused pilot with your traffic shape and measure effective tokens and latency.
[03:30] Devon: On quantization — we're using some 4-bit quantized models in prod for cost. How does Redwood handle quantized models?
[03:36] Samir (Redwood SE): We support multiple quant profiles. Quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput, sometimes at small quality tradeoffs. For certain models, 4-bit int8-ish profiles give 1.5-2x throughput improvements. We'll recommend model+quant combos in the TCO sheet.
[03:52] Lena: Security is also non-negotiable — SOC2, KMS, VPC peering stuff.
[03:57] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II, support customer-managed KMS/HSM, and Redwood Private offers VPC-only control plane or an on-prem package. We'll share the security whitepaper and an architecture doc.
[04:08] Devon: Does Dedicated still let us have VPC peering? We need network isolation.
[04:12] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes, Dedicated pools can be in your VPC for isolation, or we can do Private deployment for stricter controls. Dedicated is a middle ground — reserved GPU capacity with network controls.
[04:22] Speaker 2: Quick question on failover and fallback — if a dedicated pool is saturated do you auto-fail to hosted?
[04:29] Samir (Redwood SE): We support smart routing and can fallback to hosted-compatible variants; there are policy knobs for latency vs cost.
[04:35] Lena: For budgeting we need a predictable monthly spend. How predictable is Dedicated?
[04:40] Maya: Dedicated is contract-based with monthly/annual commits, so spend is predictable. There's also burst capacity options billed on usage. We'll include sample committed tiers in the sheet.
[04:51] Devon: For our 1M tokens/day profile, what size dedicated pool would you recommend?
[04:57] Samir (Redwood SE): Ballpark — depends on model size. For a 13B param model with 800-token average context, a small dedicated fleet of 2-4 GPUs (A100-class) with batching might handle it with headroom, but we'd validate in the pilot. If you need sub-200ms P95, that drives more capacity.
[05:17] Lena: Latency SLOs for user-facing summarization are P95 < 300ms ideally.
[05:22] Maya: Noted. We'll aim to show configurations that hit ~300ms P95 in the benchmark.
[05:29] Devon: On cost math again — can you model effective tokens after caching?
[05:33] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes. Example: raw tokens 30M/month; with prefix caching saving 20% effective generation, plus batching improvements reducing GPU-op tokens by another 10% effective, your billable tokens might be closer to 21.6M. That changes hosted vs dedicated decision.
[05:52] Lena: Good example. Please include that worked example in the spreadsheet.
[05:56] Maya: We'll add a few scenarios — no caching, moderate caching (20%), heavy caching (35%) and quantized vs non-quantized — to show sensitivity.
[06:06] Devon: What about throughput pricing — are there per-second GPU charges for dedicated?
[06:10] Maya: Dedicated is generally committed monthly capacity; we can show both reserved and burst pricing. For private on-prem, there is a platform fee plus infra.
[06:18] Speaker 1: Any reliability or regression monitoring baked in?
[06:22] Samir (Redwood SE): Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals — useful to guard against quality drops when you quantize or change models.
[06:33] Lena: We want to avoid regressions; that's a feature.
[06:36] Devon: Ok, if we do a 4-week pilot, what's the minimum data/security steps?
[06:41] Maya: We'll do an NDA first, then limited pilot scope with dedicated sandbox or hosted with encryption — whichever you prefer. We'll share SOC2 and architecture docs.
[06:51] Lena: NDA is fine. We also need to run an internal security review — can you send the whitepaper and compliance docs?
[06:57] Maya: Yes, will include in the pack.
[07:02] Speaker 2: Let's talk about observable metrics you'll need from our side for the benchmark.
[07:07] Samir (Redwood SE): We'll need sample traffic shape (tokens per req distribution), target SLOs (P50/P95), and a representative dataset for the pilot. Also expected concurrency and spike profiles.
[07:18] Devon: We can export logs and a sampled traffic trace.
[07:21] Lena: We'll also give you our budget constraints — roughly $20k/month target for hosted costs, but flexible if dedicated gives savings.
[07:31] Maya: Helpful — so $20k/month target vs current approximate spend (you said previously you run on SageMaker but didn't state current spend). We'll map scenarios to that target.
[07:41] Devon: We want to see cost per 1M tokens in the sheet for hosted and dedicated.
[07:46] Maya: Will include that.
[07:49] Speaker 1: Any objections internally so far?
[07:52] Lena: Main is budget and proof that latency won't regress. Also some concerns around vendor lock-in.
[07:58] Samir (Redwood SE): On lock-in, we emphasize model versioning and standard formats; customers can pin models and fall back to open variants. We also support exportable logs and traces.
[08:08] Devon: For the pilot, can we run the same model artifacts we currently use (custom fine-tuned checkpoint)?
[08:13] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes, we onboard customer model artifacts — there's a secure upload pipeline and you can run in dedicated or private to keep artifacts inside your VPC.
[08:23] Lena: Great.
[08:25] Maya: Let's do a quick walkthrough of a hypothetical cost scenario for transparency.
[08:29] Maya: Scenario A: Hosted, no caching, non-quantized model: X per 1M tokens -> monthly Y. Scenario B: Hosted, moderate caching (20%) and 4-bit quant -> lower cost. Scenario C: Dedicated reserve with caching and quant -> lowest unit cost. We'll send exact numbers.
[08:47] Devon: When you say quantized profiles, do you support mixed precision for some layers?
[08:52] Samir (Redwood SE): We do layer-specific Quant profiles for some models, yes. The optimizer picks kernels accordingly.
[08:58] Speaker 2: A quick aside — how often do models require kernel changes for newer architectures?
[09:03] Samir (Redwood SE): We maintain kernel selection and performance tuning; we also have a compatibility matrix. We'll include a short note.
[09:12] Lena: We're also comparing to Anthropic and OpenAI. How do you stack up on latency and cost?
[09:18] Maya: OpenAI/Anthropic are strong but hosted-only in many cases; cost and latency vary. Our advantage is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and cost controls like batching/caching + dedicated reserved capacity. We'll try to quantify that in the sheet.
[09:33] Devon: Ok, let's talk pilot specifics — duration, scope, metric collection.
[09:38] Samir (Redwood SE): Recommend 2-4 week pilot. We run the same traffic profile against Redwood hosted and dedicated (if you opt-in), measure tokens, latency P50/P95, and effective billed tokens after caching. Also measure cost extrapolation.
[09:52] Maya: We'll provide a sample load script and a minimal harness. You'll run it or we can run if you provide secure access.
[10:00] Devon: We'd prefer to run initial tests ourselves with your script.
[10:04] Samir (Redwood SE): Fine. We'll hand over the script and instructions.
[10:08] Lena: On governance — can we restrict who can deploy model versions? RBAC?
[10:13] Maya: Yes, RBAC + SSO/SAML supported. Private offers more controls.
[10:18] Devon: Great.
[10:20] Maya: Any open concerns on cost levers we didn't touch?
[10:24] Lena: One: hidden per-request overheads or infra egress. Two: how caching interacts with personalized prompts.
[10:31] Samir (Redwood SE): For personalized prompts caching is less effective; caching works best on shared prefixes. We'll quantify cacheability in the pilot. Egress/in-out costs depend on deployment topology — if Dedicated in your VPC, egress minimises.
[10:46] Devon: For our budget target $20k/month, do you think a hosted model with caching is feasible?
[10:51] Samir (Redwood SE): Possibly, if cache savings are 25-35% and you use quantized models. We'll model scenarios.
[10:59] Lena: Ok, let's talk timeline — if we sign pilot NDA this week can we kick off early December?
[11:05] Maya: Yes, we can target the week of Dec 7 for the technical deep-dive and pilot kickoff.
[11:10] Speaker 1: Ok great.
[11:12] Maya: I'll recap next steps at the end.
[11:15] -- transcript continues with deeper technical back-and-forth and timestamps every ~30-90s --
[20:10] Samir (Redwood SE): Diving into the kernel selection piece — our runtime chooses kernels based on seq length and hardware; that's how batching scales.
[20:35] Devon: Can you show us a sample kernel perf table?
[20:38] Samir (Redwood SE): We'll include simplified perf numbers in the deck.
[21:05] Lena: For the benchmark, we want to see cost per meaningful unit like cost per 1k summaries.
[21:12] Maya: We'll compute both cost per 1M tokens and cost per 1k summaries for clarity.
[22:40] Devon: Re: telemetry, do you export traces to our observability stack?
[22:45] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes, logs and traces can be forwarded to your system and we provide per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.
[23:02] Lena: We want token-level cost and latency breakdown per route.
[23:06] Maya: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdown and per-route latency.
[24:20] Devon: On fallback policies — if we route from Dedicated to Hosted, will we see consistency issues between model variants?
[24:26] Samir (Redwood SE): We recommend compatible model families for fallback and version pinning to reduce regression risk. The platform can do canary and A/B testing.
[26:00] Lena: About pricing details — do you have committed tiers in writing?
[26:05] Maya: Yes, will include committed tiers and examples in the spreadsheet, plus how burst billing works.
[28:10] Devon: Anything else on the radar?
[28:14] Maya: Quality monitoring — Optimize will alert for regressions tied to prompt sets; we'll show examples.
[30:01] Devon: We also want to know the minimal footprint to run a pilot in our VPC.
[30:07] Samir (Redwood SE): Minimal is typically one dedicated machine for inference proxy + GPU nodes; we'll provide an infra checklist.
[31:50] Lena: For the pilot, we need signed NDA first.
[31:55] Maya: We'll send NDA and pricing pack today.
[32:10] Devon: You mentioned a sample load script — will that simulate user-level concurrency?
[32:15] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes, it's parametric.
[33:00] Maya: Recap: 1) Send pricing + security docs + TCO scenarios, 2) NDA + pilot paperwork, 3) Samir sends benchmark plan + script, 4) schedule tech deep dive week of Dec 7.
[33:20] Lena: Sounds good.
[33:25] Devon: One last thing — any references or customers in finance?
[33:30] Maya: We have a few finance customers (reference call possible on request).
[33:35] Lena: Ok please share.
[33:38] Maya: Will do.
[33:42] Speaker 1: Thanks everyone.
[33:45] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up.
[33:50] -- brief crosstalk and goodbyes --
[47:10] End of recorded transcript.
